name: Standard Scramble
approach: Start at the Rachel Lake Trailhead (Trail #1313, elev. ~2,800 ft) at the end of Box Canyon Road/FR-4930. Follow the Rachel Lake Trail as it climbs gently through forest along the Box Canyon Creek drainage — the grade is easy and well-graded here, mostly Class 1 hiking. At roughly 2–2.2 miles and about 450–500 ft of gain (~3,300 ft elevation), the trail crosses a brushy avalanche-path clearing where Hibox's summit block comes into view on the ridge to the northeast; this clearing is the key landmark. Just past it (some parties note it's after the second such clearing), watch on the right/climber's-right side of the trail for an unmarked but well-established boot path (the 'Hibox climbers' path') leaving the maintained trail and heading northeast/uphill into the forest — it's easy to walk past if you're not looking for it. From here the character changes completely: the bootpath climbs steeply (mostly Class 2, with fallen timber to step over) for about 500 vertical feet before breaking out of the trees near a band of cliffs around 5,300 ft. Stay right of this first rock band, then work left around a rock outcrop, continuing through patchy timber to a second, higher cliff band; a gully on the right provides passage through it. Above this the trail opens into a large sloping subalpine meadow (wildflowers in season) that funnels into a loose talus/scree slope — this is the most tedious and slip-prone section of the route, so careful foot placement matters more than pace. A thready boot path threads up through the talus to the south side of the summit block. There is no reliable water past the lower forest/creek section, so carry what you need from the car or treat water low on the mountain. The route-finding through the two cliff bands and the avalanche-path junction low on the trail are the two spots parties most often go astray; a GPS track or recent trip report beta is worth having.

itinerary.cal: Snow-free and easiest roughly July through October; the boot path can hold snow into early summer in big years, so check recent trip reports before a June/early-July attempt.

days.note: Hike the Rachel Lake Trail to the first avalanche clearing, pick up the unmarked but well-used Hibox boot path climbing north up steep timber and talus onto Box Ridge, then follow the ridge crest east to a short Class 3 scramble on solid rock at the summit block. Reverse the same line to descend. Snow-free bootpath is easy to follow in summer season; the whole outing is a long single day, not an overnight.
days.title: Rachel Lake to Hibox summit, car-to-car

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Start at ~2,800 ft on the Rachel Lake Trail (FR 4930 trailhead).

schedule.label: Reach boot-path junction
schedule.detail: About 2 mi in, near the first avalanche clearing where the unmarked Hibox climbers' path breaks off north.

schedule.label: Top out on Box Ridge
schedule.detail: Steep, sustained boot path through timber and loose talus gains the ridge crest.

schedule.label: Summit block
schedule.detail: Short Class 3 scramble on solid rock to the 6,548 ft summit; broad views of Rampart Ridge and the Stuart Range.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the boot path down Box Ridge to the Rachel Lake Trail.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Total roughly 8-9 hours car-to-car for a fit party.

days.objective: Summit Hibox Mountain via Box Ridge boot path

itinerary.totalNote: A single long day car-to-car: ~7 mi round trip, 3,900 ft gain, typically 6-10 hours depending on pace and summit time — this is not an overnight trip for the standard route.
